answers.reason: The student holds no office and does not take part in central university governance bodies.
The student holds no administrative or leadership office responsible for the university budget.
The student holds no office and is not involved in selecting candidates for professorships.
Ordinary students are represented by the elected student representative and do not sit on the faculty council themselves.
Student representation in faculty committees is handled by the elected student representative, not by a student holding no office.
Although the board decides on individual students' matters, a student holding no office is not a member of the board.
The student is enrolled in a bachelor programme and is not involved in awarding research grants.
Rewriting module descriptions is a task for teaching staff and relevant representatives, not an ordinary student without office.
The student has no role in procuring laboratory equipment.
Every member has one place where their matters are decided, and orientation week planning is the informal student-level round where an ordinary student without office can take part.
